method: Untimed local geometry observed in cached native zoom-20 aerial imagery. GoPro picture-only crops confirm maneuver and branch identity. No camera GPS, receiver speed, mean GPS, or error score used to choose paths. Coordinates below are east/north meter offsets from each origin. Envelopes and obstacle cores are approximate independent visual checks, not surveyed lane boundaries or vehicle-footprint certification.

sites.label: 1-2: parking-lot departure
sites.note: Initial heading comes from the northbound parking aisle, not a previous lap or a stationary point. Go north past the island, then west. End positions differ legitimately between laps.

sites.label: 54-55: N 10th fork
sites.note: Follow the right-hand through branch around the painted/physical splitter. Keep intermediate blinker anchors on laps 2 and 3. Construction cones in the drive differ from the aerial scene: branch alignment is supported, exact temporary lane center is uncertain.

sites.label: 58-59: shallow intersection crossing
sites.note: Use the visible local northbound alignment and the start tangent of the corrected N 10th guide; the far end of the 300+ m road bend is not the exit heading of this crossing.

sites.label: 60-61: outer roundabout exit
sites.note: Join the corrected approach and exit with their local tangents. The previous curve was almost northbound at an east-northeast entry. Original entry-anchor/paint conflicts on laps 2 and 3 remain flagged; no original click is moved.

sites.label: 83-84: Antelope / Holdrege crossing
sites.note: Continue the local through-lane direction between the two corrected guides. Do not use the distant end of the downstream Antelope bend, which produces a false hook.

sites.label: 119-121: parking-lot return
sites.note: One turn can contain begin-stop/finish-stop anchors. Preserve the hold and every original anchor, travel east below the parking island, then turn north on its east side. Use each lap's endpoints directly rather than deforming a shared endpoint into an S bend. The 1.6 m pre-stop displacement on lap 2 remains a straight anchor connection with uncertain heading. Low-confidence lap-1 clicks remain low confidence.
